Acknowledge the frustration first — empathy lowers the temperature before you solve anything.
Gather facts (delivery details, notes, likely safe spots) before guessing what happened.
If a package truly can't be located, point the customer to the official support/claims process.

"Wasn't me — I don't even run this route on Mondays. You'd have to take it up with whoever did."

Lead with empathy, not with who's to blame.
"Ma'am, I need you to calm down before we can talk about this."

Never tell an upset customer to "calm down" — acknowledge how they feel instead.

"Here — just take this one I'm holding. It'll even out."

Never give a customer someone else's package to smooth things over.

"Glad we found it! You can add delivery instructions to your account so drivers use the front porch."
